title: Every Scripture is God-breathed
author: 2 Timothy
lines: and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction,
that each person who belongs to God may be complete,
thoroughly equipped for every good work.
why: Paul's last letter, to his younger friend Timothy, says what the Scriptures are for: not to win arguments, but to teach, correct and train, so that a person is ready for every good work. It is the New Testament's own short account of what the Bible is and does.

title: Open my eyes
author: Psalms
lines: that I may see wondrous things out of your law.
why: A one-line prayer from the longest psalm, for the moment before you read. It assumes that the wonders are already in the text, and that what is missing is sight. Jews and Christians have prayed it before reading Scripture for centuries.

title: Doers of the word
author: James
lines: But be doers of the word,
why: The letter of James, the most practical book in the New Testament, says that hearing without doing is a kind of self-deception. It is the test of every way of reading the Bible: what do you do next?
